title: Order and effort
hookLine: all is within the hukam, yet the Gurus ask us to strive
last: BEYOND EVERY SKY, AND THE LIGHT WITHIN ALL.

lines: IF ALL IS ORDERED, WHY TRY?
cards: A farmer in Punjab can't make it rain. She can't choose the heat, or the day the monsoon arrives, or whether a storm flattens the wheat a week before harvest.
And still, every season, she's up before light: plowing, sowing, watering, mending the channel where the water runs.
Nobody would call her lazy for not controlling the sky, and nobody would call her wise for sitting in the doorway waiting for it.
Sikh thought takes her life seriously as a question: if everything happens within God's order, why try?

teach.h: HUKAM: NO ONE IS OUTSIDE IT.
teach.b: Hukam is the Granth's word for the order: the command, the will, the way the One runs everything. In year one you met it as living in tune.
In the second pauri of Japji, Guru Nanak says, in paraphrase: by hukam all forms are made; by hukam some are high and some low, some get joy and some get pain.
Then the line that leaves no gaps: everyone is within the hukam, and no one is outside it. And yet the same scripture is full of work.

teach.h: MAKE THE EFFORT, LIVE IN PEACE.
teach.b: Guru Arjan says, in paraphrase: make the effort, and earning by it, live in peace; meditating, you meet the Lord. Sikh life is built on this.
Kirat karo, earn an honest living, is one of the pillars Sikhs name beside remembering the Name and sharing. How do the two fit?

teach.h: NOT A SCRIPT, A SKY TO WORK UNDER.
teach.b: Sikh teachers say hukam isn't fate in the sense of a script you sit and watch. It's closer to the farmer's sky: the frame you live inside. Your effort is part of the order, not a fight against it.
Japji's answer to how to live is, in paraphrase, to walk in the way of the hukam. Walking is still walking; you still lift your feet. That takes a weight off.
If everything hung on your effort alone, every failure would be total. If nothing did, there'd be no reason to get up.

teach.h: DO YOUR PART; LET THE REST BE.
teach.b: Within the order, you do your part fully, and let the rest be what it is.

how: Sikhs recite Japji Sahib, which says all are within the hukam, each morning, and they hold honest work, kirat karo, alongside remembering the Name and sharing as part of daily Sikh life.

o: a rule that hard work alone earns every good thing
your honest effort as part of God's order, not against it
a fate already written, so effort changes nothing

games.q: order and effort: tap the pairs.
p: the command, the will, the order
no one is outside the hukam
make the effort, live in peace

s: because all is within the hukam, Sikh teaching says effort is pointless
the Gurus ask for honest work and striving; effort is part of the order.
Japji says no one is outside the hukam
everyone is within it, Guru Nanak says in the second pauri.
kirat karo, honest work, is named alongside remembering the Name and sharing
Sikhs name these together as pillars of daily life.

games.q: you're a farmer, and you can't control the rain. the season is starting. what do you do?
o: sit in the doorway; it's all in God's hands anyway.
plow and sow, and leave the sky to the order.
refuse to plant until the weather is certain.
games.why: the Gurus ask for striving within the hukam: do your part fully, and let the rest be.

practice: Bring one worry to mind and gently split it in two: the part that's yours, a call, a task, an apology, and the part that isn't, other people's choices, the weather, the outcome.
Choose one small piece from your side, and with each out-breath set the other side down.

wordCard.voice: Order and effort. Everything is within the hukam, and still the Gurus ask for honest work and striving: your effort is part of the order. Today's word.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: command, will, order: the way the One runs everything.

carryVoice: Your line: strive within the order. The sky isn't yours; the plowing is. See you tomorrow.

sources.ref: Ang 522 (Gujri ki Var, slok, Guru Arjan)
